titleText.es: ¿Completamente implausible? Sí. Sin embargo, merece la pena tener un bote de repelente de tiburones al lado de la cama.
titleText.en: Completely implausible? Yes. Nevertheless, worth keeping a can of shark repellent next to the bed.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish raster translates the dialogue and changes the official sound effects SPLOOSH, CLICK, HISSS, and CHOMP CHOMP to SPLAASH, CLIC, SSSSSS, and ÑAM ÑAM. It leaves CHUNK unchanged, so CHUNK is excluded while the localized sounds are taught. The Spanish image also uses singular LA CÁPSULA where the official image says THE CAPSULES, and it omits the official capsule's small IF FOUND PLEASE CALL label; this artifact follows the Spanish image exactly. The title and title text preserve the joke about science outreach accidentally carrying a live shark to the public.

regions.labelEs: EL DISPOSITIVO DE SEGUIMIENTO REGISTRARÁ LOS MOVIMIENTOS Y HÁBITOS DEL TIBURÓN.

applications.explanationEn: De seguimiento gives the device's tracking purpose, where English normally uses tracking directly before device.
The future ending -á is attached to the complete dictionary form registrar.

regions.labelEs: LUEGO SE SOLTARÁ Y SUBIRÁ HASTA LA SUPERFICIE.

applications.explanationEn: Se presents the device as coming free, and soltará places that change in the future.
The future ending -á follows the full form soltar.
The future ending -á follows the full form subir.

regions.labelEs: NO NOS PODEMOS PERMITIR UN PROGRAMA DE RECUPERACIÓN, ASÍ QUE LA CÁPSULA INFLARÁ UN GLOBO DE HELIO, FLOTARÁ SOBRE LA TIERRA,

applications.explanationEn: No negates the expression; nos identifies the group that lacks the resources; podemos carries the changed verb and permitir remains unchanged.
Podemos carries the person and time, while permitir stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
The two words form one connector that introduces the result of not funding retrieval.
De helio identifies the gas inside the balloon rather than ownership.
The future ending -á follows the complete form inflar.
The future ending -á follows the complete form flotar despite the printed line break.

regions.labelEs: Y CON SUERTE ALGUIEN LA ENCONTRARÁ Y NOS LA MANDARÁ POR CORREO.

applications.explanationEn: The fixed two-word expression introduces the hoped-for outcome.
La replaces the feminine capsule and appears directly before the future verb encontrará.
La replaces the feminine capsule and appears directly before mandará.
Nos identifies the recipients and stands before the future verb mandará; la appears between them because it identifies the thing sent rather than the recipient.
Nos identifies the recipients, la identifies the feminine capsule, and both precede the changed verb in that order.
Por introduces correo as the channel used to return the capsule.
The future ending -á follows the complete dictionary form encontrar.
The future ending -á follows the complete form mandar.

excludedUnits.rationale: CHUNK is retained unchanged from the English source rather than localized as Spanish curriculum text.
The three exclamation marks show the shark's reaction but are not a Spanish lexical unit.
The curved marks and circle depict vibration or inflation around the device rather than a Spanish word.
The two question marks convey confusion but are not a Spanish lexical unit.

applications.explanationEn: Quiero carries the person and present time, while ser remains in its unchanged dictionary form.
The bare profession follows ser without una because it has no added description.

cards.noteEn: Dispositivo names a piece of equipment made for a particular purpose.

example.en: The device measures the temperature.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “tracking device” in Spanish?
cards.noteEn: Spanish uses de to connect the device to its purpose. English commonly places tracking directly before device instead.

example.es: Colocaron un dispositivo de seguimiento en la caja.
example.en: They put a tracking device on the box.

cards.promptEs: dispositivo de seguimiento · tiburón · globo de helio · científica
cards.answerEn: The tracking capsule is supposed to detach from the shark, inflate a helium balloon, cross land, and be returned by mail. It fails to detach, so the balloon carries the shark to people instead; the disastrous demonstration still inspires a child to become a scientist.
cards.noteEn: The official title Outreach refers both to presenting science to the public and to the apparatus literally reaching the public. The title text extends the airborne-shark absurdity by recommending shark repellent beside the bed.

cards.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’

example.en: I need a coffee cup.

cards.noteEn: Registrará is the future form of registrar for one person or thing.

example.en: The sensor will record every change.

cards.questionEn: How do you say what someone will do in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Keep the action verb in its dictionary form and add a future ending such as -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, or -án.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. The ending identifies the person: sentir plus -á gives sentirá, and ver plus -á gives verá. A few common verbs change their stem, but use the same endings.

example.en: Marta will call tomorrow.

cards.noteEn: Movimientos is the plural of movimiento and can describe changes in position or a path followed over time.

example.es: La cámara sigue los movimientos del animal.
example.en: The camera follows the animal's movements.

cards.noteEn: Hábitos are repeated behaviors or routines. The written accent remains in the plural.

example.es: Estudian los hábitos nocturnos de las aves.
example.en: They study the birds' nighttime habits.

cards.noteEn: Spanish writes de followed by the masculine singular word el as the single word del.

example.es: El color del coche es rojo.
example.en: The color of the car is red.

cards.noteEn: Tiburón is the general Spanish word for a shark.

example.es: Vieron un tiburón cerca del barco.
example.en: They saw a shark near the boat.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; presents the thing as changing
cards.noteEn: With verbs such as reducir and ampliar, se lets Spanish describe a change without naming anyone who causes it. English often uses a simple verb such as “shrinks” or “widens.”

example.en: The stain shrinks.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that an object comes loose or detaches?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of soltarse.
cards.noteEn: The short pronoun changes with the subject and comes before a finite verb: la pieza se suelta, las piezas se soltaron. The dictionary form keeps se attached: soltarse.

example.es: La etiqueta se soltó durante el viaje.
example.en: The label came loose during the trip.

cards.noteEn: Soltará is a future form of soltar. With se, it can describe something detaching or coming free without naming a person who releases it.

example.es: La pieza se soltará con el movimiento.
example.en: The piece will come loose with the movement.

cards.noteEn: Subirá is the future form of subir for one person or thing.

example.en: The balloon will rise slowly.

cards.noteEn: Before a place, hasta marks the endpoint reached by movement. English often uses simply to, while as far as makes the endpoint emphasis explicit.

example.en: We walked to the station.

cards.noteEn: Superficie is the outside or upper level of something, including the top of a body of water.

example.es: La boya volvió a la superficie.
example.en: The buoy returned to the surface.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone cannot afford something?
cards.answerEn: Use no, a matching form of poder, and permitirse.
cards.noteEn: The person pronoun from permitirse normally appears before the changed form of poder: no me puedo permitir, no nos podemos permitir. The thing that is unaffordable follows the expression.

example.es: No me puedo permitir un viaje este año.
example.en: I cannot afford a trip this year.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; marks a “we” verb that is used with nos
cards.noteEn: Some Spanish verbs conventionally come with me, te, se, nos, or os even when no one literally acts on themselves. Nos marks the form for a group that includes the speaker. English usually absorbs it into the verb's meaning.

example.en: We complain about the noise.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

example.en: We can enter now.

cards.noteEn: In poder permitirse algo, permitir is part of the expression for having enough money, time, or resources for something. This differs from permitir meaning to allow.

example.en: We cannot afford another expense.

cards.noteEn: Here programa is a planned set of activities or services, not a computer program.

example.es: La ciudad creó un programa de reciclaje.
example.en: The city created a recycling program.

cards.noteEn: Recuperación can mean getting an object back as well as returning to health or a previous condition.

example.es: La recuperación del equipo tardó dos días.
example.en: Retrieving the equipment took two days.

cards.answerEn: so; therefore (as part of así que)

cards.questionEn: How do you connect a situation to its result with “so”?
cards.answerEn: Use así que before the result.
cards.noteEn: Así que joins a cause or situation to what follows from it. The two words work together as one connector; translating así and que separately will not give the intended meaning.

example.es: Está lloviendo, así que llevo un paraguas.
example.en: It is raining, so I am carrying an umbrella.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of a result connector

cards.noteEn: Cápsula can be a small sealed container that protects equipment or material.

example.en: The capsule protects the instrument.

cards.noteEn: Inflará is the future form of inflar for one person or thing.

example.en: The pump will inflate the balloon.

cards.noteEn: Globo can name a small rubber balloon or a larger balloon used to rise through the air.

example.es: El globo ascendió sobre el campo.
example.en: The balloon rose over the field.

cards.questionEn: How do you name a balloon filled with helium?
cards.noteEn: De links the balloon to the gas inside it. English usually places helium directly before balloon.

example.es: El globo de helio llegó al techo.
example.en: The helium balloon reached the ceiling.

cards.noteEn: Helio is the light chemical element used to make some balloons rise.

example.en: They filled the balloon with helium.

cards.noteEn: Flotará is the future form of flotar for one person or thing.

example.es: La boya flotará hasta la costa.
example.en: The buoy will float to the coast.

cards.noteEn: Sobre can introduce the geographical area across which something is measured or happens. This is different from sobre meaning ‘about’ a topic.

example.es: La tormenta avanza sobre la costa.
example.en: The storm moves over the coast.

cards.noteEn: This sense contrasts land with the sea. It does not name the planet Earth or soil as a material.

example.es: Después de horas en el mar, vimos tierra.
example.en: After hours at sea, we saw land.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a hoped-for result with “hopefully” or “with luck”?
cards.noteEn: Con suerte comments on the chance that the following event will happen. It can appear at the beginning or inside a sentence.

example.es: Con suerte, llegaremos antes de la lluvia.
example.en: With luck, we will arrive before the rain.

cards.promptEs: lo, la, los, las delante de un verbo conjugado
cards.questionEn: Where do you put the Spanish word for “it” or “them” when the main verb already shows who acts and when?
cards.answerEn: Put lo, la, los, or las directly before that verb.
cards.noteEn: These short words replace the person or thing directly affected by the action; that role is called the direct object. Choose lo or los for a masculine thing, la or las for a feminine thing, and match singular or plural. Before a verb form such as conté or vimos, write the short word separately in front: lo conté, las vimos. With an unchanged dictionary form, it can instead attach to the end, as in verlo.

example.en: The movie—we watched it yesterday.

cards.noteEn: Encontrará is the future form of encontrar for one person or thing.

example.en: Someone will find the box.

cards.promptEs: me/te/le/nos/os/les delante del verbo que cambia
cards.questionEn: Where do you put the short word that identifies who receives something?
cards.answerEn: Put me, te, le, nos, os, or les before the first verb that changes for the person and time.
cards.noteEn: The slashes in the prompt mean to choose the one receiver word that fits. A verb that changes for the person and time is often called a conjugated verb: estoy rather than the dictionary form estar. In a multiword verb phrase, the receiver word goes before that changed verb, so les estoy enviando places les before estoy, not between estoy and enviando.

example.en: I am sending them a photo.

cards.questionEn: How do you order a person pronoun and a thing pronoun before a verb that changes for person and time?
cards.answerEn: Put the person pronoun first, the thing pronoun second, and both before the changed verb.
cards.noteEn: The slashes mean to choose one item, and the plus signs show the order. For example, nos la mandará places nos for the recipients before la for the feminine thing. Before lo, la, los, or las, le and les change to se.

example.en: They will send it to us tomorrow.

cards.noteEn: Mandará is the future form of mandar for one person or thing. Mandar can mean to send an object or message.

example.es: Marta nos mandará la foto mañana.
example.en: Marta will send us the photo tomorrow.

cards.noteEn: Por can identify the channel used to communicate: por teléfono, por radio, or por videollamada. Natural English often uses ‘on,’ ‘by,’ or ‘over’ rather than translating por with one fixed word.

example.en: We talk by video call.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something is sent or received by mail?
cards.noteEn: Por introduces the delivery or communication channel. Correo can refer to postal mail or email; the surrounding context tells which one.

example.es: Te enviaré el contrato por correo.
example.en: I will send you the contract by mail.

cards.noteEn: This sense of correo is the physical postal service used for letters and parcels. Correo electrónico or email identifies electronic mail when the distinction matters.

example.en: The letter arrived by mail.

cards.noteEn: Splaash is a stretched comic-book sound for a large object entering water. The extra a suggests a longer or larger splash.

example.en: The rock fell into the water: splash!

cards.noteEn: A run of s letters can represent a sustained hiss, such as air leaving a valve or filling a balloon.

example.en: The valve went “hissss.”

cards.noteEn: A long run of a letters represents a sustained scream. The number of letters varies with the desired length or intensity.

example.en: A long scream was heard from the hallway.

cards.noteEn: Ñam is a common Spanish sound for taking a bite or eating eagerly. Repeating it suggests repeated bites.

example.es: El niño miró el pastel y dijo: «¡Ñam!».
example.en: The child looked at the cake and said, “Yum!”

cards.noteEn: Papi is an affectionate, familiar way to address or refer to one's father.

example.en: Daddy, can I ask you a question?

cards.questionEn: How do you say what someone wants to do?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of querer, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Querer changes to match the person and time, while the desired action stays unchanged: quiero salir, quieres comer, queremos dormir. Spanish does not insert a between the two verbs.

example.en: Lucía wants to rest.

cards.promptEs: ser + profesión, relación o rol sin un/una
cards.questionEn: When you say someone's profession, relationship, or role in Spanish, do you always need a word for “a” or “an”?
cards.answerEn: Often no. Use a form of ser directly before the profession, relationship, or role when it has no added description.
cards.noteEn: Ser changes to match the person: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, or son. A bare profession or role normally follows without un or una: soy estudiante. An article commonly returns when the noun has an added description or is being singled out: es una estudiante excelente.

example.en: Luis is a teacher.

cards.noteEn: As a noun, científica names a woman or girl who works in science. The matching masculine form is científico.

example.en: Ana wants to be a scientist.
